body: Channel-off check fires from on_chunk when a stream read reaches the end of the transcript (!more && !stopped, or missing file) channel_wait after the hand-over, not from a separate on_tick deadline; the stream's own next_read deadline drives it. Alternative rejected: a tick deadline would notify while the stream lags behind Telegram backpressure (record not read yet) -> false notice.

Only sessions with a stream target (agent with transcript_reads bound to the session) are watched; alternative of watching every live agent and relying on hooks alone rejected: UserPromptSubmit for channel messages is unverified (INBOUND_SETTLE note), a long no-tool turn would look like a dead channel.

Container detection: /.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv, env container=, /proc/1/cgroup; the e2e test fakes it with env container=docker (a real Podman/nspawn sign). Alternative rejected: an installer-only override variable used only by tests.

CI run 1, macOS container test: install.sh in_container returns false on macOS (a Mac is never a container; Docker there runs Linux; the macOS branch writes the stable LocalHostName). Alternative rejected: only skip the container steps in the test on macOS, which would keep the script printing 'in a container' and then writing the Mac's name anyway.

CI run 1, ubuntu console test: the race is test-side (ingress answers registered after events.send, before the actor binds the agent; control is another channel), so the test waits for the topic's alive icon via Hub::agent_bound, also in a_late_key_answer which a 300 ms probe also broke. Alternative rejected: answering registered only after the actor bound the agent (protocol change for a race no real agent is exposed to: console commands come from Telegram, not from the agent).

CI run 1, macOS permission hook test: event-driven wait (prompt shown or hook ended) and up to 3 hook runs with the hook's stderr in the failure. Alternative rejected: raising PERMISSION_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (product constant; keeps a stopped hub cheap for Claude Code on Windows).

Probe PERMISSION_CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 0 did not make the hook time out: tokio::time::timeout polls the inner future first and the loopback connect and send finished on the first poll. A 600 ms sleep inside the send future reproduced the CI symptom instead.
